text: Aurel hated sitting still.
The painter gave up in the end.
Painted him about to laugh.
That's how I remember him. About to.
Twelve years a fire-warden in the lower wards.
You learn to read a fire the way clerks read a ledger.
Where it started. How fast. Who wanted it.
Corwen's Wharf burned on a calm night.
No wind. No lightning.
Fires don't start themselves on calm nights.
This one started in three places at once.
Aurel was inside.
Doing the inventory the owner asked him to do.
On a Sunday night.
It was insured for twice what it was worth.
The magistrate called it an accident.
Took him a week.
The owner bought a house in the hills that autumn.
I went to his party once.
I wasn't invited.
The Quiet Office found me the week they closed the case.
Officially, we're crown auditors.
Ledgers. Seals. Tariffs.
Unofficially, we read the numbers nobody wants read.
The lantern is the Office's.
It shows what magic leaves behind.
In this city, magic is something you do quietly, or not at all.
Half this city belongs to the Ahm now.
The other half owes them.
Their master laughs a lot.
Men who laugh a lot have usually bought the room.
Tyr watches from the hill.
The city watches everyone else.
Especially anyone with pointed ears.
Brann thinks every case is about money.
He's usually right.
Pell draws everything.
Even me, when he thinks I'm not looking.
Lately the numbers have started leaving bodies.
